title: Regularization for Deep Learning
learning_outcomes: Explain regularization for Deep Learning and connect at least two of its listed subtopics.
Apply the central idea in regularization for Deep Learning to a small example or select a suitable approach for a stated scenario.
Identify an important assumption, failure mode, risk, or limitation and describe how it should be checked.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study regularization for Deep Learning within Neural Networks and Deep Learning. You will connect the syllabus topics below to a small, inspectable example and practice stating what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Neural networks are parameterized functions trained by optimizing a loss. Small, inspectable experiments help reveal how data, gradients, and settings interact.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Regularization discourages brittle dependence on training examples or parameters. Dropout, weight decay, normalization, augmentation, and early stopping have different mechanics and should be evaluated rather than applied indiscriminately.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus topics covered in this lesson

items.title: Weight decay
items.text: This method changes training behavior to improve optimization or reduce overfitting. Check when it is active, what state it introduces, and whether it matches the model architecture and deployment behavior.

items.title: Dropout
items.text: This method changes training behavior to improve optimization or reduce overfitting. Check when it is active, what state it introduces, and whether it matches the model architecture and deployment behavior.

items.title: Data augmentation
items.text: Data augmentation is one of the concepts used to reason about regularization for deep learning. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Batch normalization
items.text: Scaling transforms numeric features to a common range or statistical scale. Fit scaling parameters on training data only and apply the same learned transformation to validation, test, and production inputs.

items.title: Layer normalization
items.text: Scaling transforms numeric features to a common range or statistical scale. Fit scaling parameters on training data only and apply the same learned transformation to validation, test, and production inputs.

items.title: Early stopping
items.text: Early stopping is one of the concepts used to reason about regularization for deep learning. Define the inputs, assumptions, and intended result in this context, then test the idea on a small representative example and document where it may not apply.

items.title: Choosing regularization methods
items.text: Regularization discourages overly complex solutions or improves robustness during training. Its strength is a trade-off and should be selected using development data rather than final test results.

content_blocks.title: A practical way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the task definition and the inputs available. Make the expected behavior explicit, choose a simple reference point, and inspect both ordinary examples and cases where assumptions may fail. Neural networks are parameterized functions trained by optimizing a loss. Small, inspectable experiments help reveal how data, gradients, and settings interact.

content_blocks.code:
inputs = [0.5, 1.0]
weights = [2.0, -1.0]
bias = 0.25
score = sum(x * w for x, w in zip(inputs, weights)) + bias
relu = max(0.0, score)
print("score:", round(score, 2))
print("relu:", round(relu, 2))
